newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan kills some 35 Ethiopians, rebels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sudan kills some 35 Ethiopians, rebels - paper.

text.p: The Sudanese army and militias have killed more than 35 Ethiopian mercenaries and Sudanese rebels in the east of the country and are now besieging the remainder of the force, a government paper said on Saturday.

"The armed forces and the Popular Defence Force achieved a spectacular victory yesterday on the Tigrayan (Ethiopian) mercenaries and pockets of rebels in the Khor Al-Gana area," Al-Sudan Al-Hadith said.
The Sudanese forces "managed to kill over 35 of the enemy forces," it added. "We lost three martyrs."
Ethiopian forces and rebels of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) fled, leaving behind their dead, weapons and food supplies carrying Ethiopian markings, the paper said.
"Our forces forced the Tigrayan mercenaries and pockets of rebels to retreat to where they are now besieged in a narrow border strip," it added.
Sudanese opposition forces, bent on toppling the Islamist government of Khartoum, launched just over a month ago an offensive across Sudan's eastern and southern borders.
Sudan has accused Ethiopia and Eritrea of supporting the rebel offensive. Both countries deny any involvement in the conflict and the rebels say that they alone are waging the offensive.
The Sudanese press also reported that Eritrean and Ethiopian government forces suffered heavy losses in separate attacks by rebels in the two states.
None of the reports could be independently confirmed.

The government-owned daily Al-Ingaz Al-Watani said the rebel Eritrean Liberation Front (ELF) killed 83 Eritrean forces last week in the north coast area of Ariri. Two tanks and military equipment were destroyed in the attack, it said.
Another paper, the privately-owned Akhbar Al-Youm said Ethiopian rebels waged "a fierce attack" on Ethiopian forces in the last few days.
"The (Ethiopian) government forces sustained huge losses in the attack during which an arms store ... was seized," the paper said.
